subject: Second-Order Factor Measurement Invariance MGCFA - Releasing Parameters

messages.author: d3be9fddce1fcaa2
messages.subject: Second-Order Factor Measurement Invariance MGCFA - Releasing Parameters
parts:
Hi all, 

I am testing measurement invariance in a second-order CFA model, with 4 first-order factors. I am using the measEQ.syntax in R to test for scalar invariance between two age groups. I've established metric invariance in the second-order factor (constraining both first- and second-order factor loadings) and scalar invariance for the first-order factors. 

The second-order factor is not invariant at the scalar level and I am trying to free 2 parameters based on the the lavTestScore results. However, I am getting an error message when using "group.partial". Below is my code and the error message when I try to run it. Can someone help me out with what I might be doing wrong?

```{r}
scalar_higher <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = higherorder_model,
              data = data,
              estimator = "MLR",
              ID.fac = "ul",
              group = "age_group",
              group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts", "regressions", "means"),
              group.partial = c("g =~ fact2", "g ~ 1"))
```
Error in group.partial == "" && length(group.partial) == 1L : 'length = 2' in coercion to 'logical(1)'

Sorry this is the first time I am posting in this group (and doing higher-order MGCFA). Please let me know if you need more information. 

Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: Second-Order Factor Measurement Invariance MGCFA - Releasing Parameters
parts: The second-order factor is not invariant at the scalar level and I am trying to free 2 parameters

Is "g" the higher-order factor?  If you provide your higherorder_model syntax, that could help, even more so with data.  Or try making a similar higher-order example using the HS data on the ?cfa help page by adding a "g" factor with 3 first-order factors.  If I can run a reprex, then I am more likely to be able to help.

Also, make sure you are using the latest development version of semTools, just in case this is an old bug that was already fixed.

remotes::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")
